entities.summary:
Jan Čapek of Sány was a Czech Hussite noble and general of Władysław III of Poland, who played a significant role in the Hussite Wars (1419-1434) and the Polish-Teutonic War (1410-1411).

As a prominent military leader, Čapek of Sány contributed to the defeat of the Teutonic Knights and the establishment of Polish independence. His victories at the Battle of Grunwald (1410) and the Battle of Tuchola (1427) showcased his military prowess and cemented his reputation as a skilled commander.

Despite his notable achievements, Čapek of Sány's legacy was overshadowed by the tumultuous history of the Hussite and Polish states. His death in 1452 marked the end of an era, but his impact on the region's politics and military strategies continued to be felt for centuries to come.

The inscription on his tombstone in Sány, Czech Republic, reads: 'He who was faithful and true, shall not be forgotten.' This poignant reminder serves as a testament to Čapek of Sány's enduring legacy as a hero of Czech and Polish history.

The Jan Čapek of Sány Museum in Sány, Czech Republic, houses a collection of artifacts and relics from his life and military campaigns, providing a glimpse into the life of this fascinating historical figure.
